nodes.name: APMS modification of GO
nodes.procedure: 1g of GO and 2ml of APMS were dispersed in 150ml of ethanol. Then, the mixture was sonicated for 30 minutes followed by stirring at 50°C for 24h. The resultant APMS modified GO was done centrifuging at 3000rpm for 40min, washed with ethanol and dried at 80°C for 24h.

nodes.name: GO/APMS/MnS2 nanocomposite formation
nodes.procedure: Equal amounts (1g) of MnS2 and APMS/GO were dispersed in 100ml of distilled water. The resultant mixture was sonicated for 30 minutes in order to obtain uniform dispersion in the solvent, followed by constant stirring using magnetic stirrer for 45 minutes. The resultant GO/APMS/MnS2 nanocomposites were cleaned with ethanol and distilled water and finally dried in hot air oven for 24h at 60°C.

nodes.name: PU-GO/APMS-MnS2 nanocomposite coating
nodes.procedure: The GO-APMS/MnS2 nanocomposites with various composition (0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 wt.%) were mixed with PU and aliphatic amine hardener with 3:1 ratio by means of stirring with 3000rpm for 2h in order to produce the stable coating formulations. The Al alloy samples were coated with pure PU, PU-MnS2, PU-APMS/MnS2, PU-GO/MnS2, and PU-GO/APMS-MnS2 nanocomposite using spin coater (Model: HSC-9999). The coated samples were dried for 7 days at room temperature. The thickness of the coating was found to be 45±5μm for all the studied coating system.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure MnS₂ nanoparticles are equally dispersed with agglomeration (Fig. 1a); APMS/MnS₂ shows reduced accumulation and uniform MnS₂ distribution due to APMS bonding (Fig. 1c); GO/APMS-MnS₂ is evenly dispersed without aggregation due to tight GO bonding (Fig. 1e).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM examinations of pure MnS₂, as-synthesized APMS/MnS₂, and GO/APMS-MnS₂ composites are shown in Figures 1(a), 1(c), and 1(e), respectively. The pure MnS₂ nanoparticles are equally dispersed with agglomeration... GO/APMS-MnS₂ is evenly dispersed without aggregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure MnS₂ (Fig. 1b) confirms Mn and S; APMS/MnS₂ (Fig. 1d) shows C, N, O, S, Mn peaks; GO/APMS-MnS₂ (Fig. 1f) shows C, N, O, S, Mn confirming effective APMS/MnS₂ inclusion into GO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figures 1b, d, and f, respectively, the elements present in pure MnS₂, as-synthesized APMS/MnS₂, and GO/APMS-MnS₂ are shown. Figure 1b shows that the Mn and S are verified... This demonstrates how APMS/MnS₂ were more effectively included into GO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure MnS₂ shows nanoscale aggregates (Fig. 2a); APMS/MnS₂ shows uniform distribution due to strong APMS binding (Fig. 2b); GO/APMS-MnS₂ shows APMS/MnS₂ tightly encased within GO sheets forming sheet-like structures (Fig. 2c).
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images of untreated pure MnS₂, as-synthesized APMS/MnS₂, and GO/APMS-MnS₂ are shown in Figs. 2a, 2b, and 2c, respectively. As can be seen in Fig. 2a, aggregates of pure MnS₂ samples are nanoscale in size.

nodes.characterization_summary: GO/APMS-MnS₂ shows sharp peak at 11.8° (002 plane of GO) and peaks at 21.8°, 32.2°, 35.5°, 38.0°, 43.1° corresponding to cubic MnS₂ (111), (210), (211), (220), (221) planes (JCPDS 25-0549) with slight shifts matching pure GO and APMS/MnS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The GO/APMS-MnS₂ showed six peaks: one sharp peak at 11.8° corresponds to hkl indices of (002) plane of GO and the other remaining five sharp peaks at 21.8°, 32.2°, 35.5°, 38.0°, and 43.1° correspond to hkl indices of (111), (210), (211), (220), and (221) planes of cubic structures of MnS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure MnS₂ stable to 600°C with 30% weight loss above; APMS/MnS₂ shows three steps: phenyl group to 270°C (6% loss), phenoxy 270-350°C (20% loss), MnO₂ formation 570-650°C (25% loss); GO/APMS-MnS₂ shows 3%, 13%, 19% losses indicating enhanced thermal stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TGA plots of pure MnS₂, as-synthesized APMS/MnS₂, and GO/APMS-MnS₂ nanocomposites are shown in Fig. 3b. It reveals that, pure MnS₂ showed weight loss around 600°C... TG curves obtained for GO/APMS-MnS₂ nanocomposites showed very less weight percentage loss of 3%, 13% and 19%.

Fig. 4a depicts XPS spectra of the C 1s state for GO/APMS-MnS₂... Fig. 4c shows the N 1s XPS spectrum... The O 1s spectra (Fig. 4c) indicate three differing interfacial oxygen states... Fig. 4d shows the Si 2p spectra at 103 eV and 101 eV... Fig. 4e shows deconvoluted peaks relating to S 2p₃/₂ and S 2p₁/₂ at 163.5 eV and 162.1 eV... Two main peaks obtained for Mn corresponding to Mn2p₁/₂, and Mn 2p₃/₂ at 654.8 eV, and 641.9 eV confirm the existence of Mn with a valence of +4.
